A football game is comprised of exactly sixty minutes of play, a basketball game forty or forty-eight minutes, but baseball has no set length of time within which the game must be completed. The pace of the game is therefore leisurely and unhurried, like the world before the discipline of measured time, deadlines, schedules, and wages paid by the hour. Baseball belongs to the kind of world in which people did not say, "I haven't got all day." Baseball games do have all day to be played. But that does not mean that they can go on forever. Baseball, like traditional life, proceeds according to the rhythm of nature, specifically the rotation of the Earth. During its first half century, games were not played at night, which meant that baseball games, like the traditional work day, ended when the sun set. If we create a routine, we don't have to expend precious energy every day prioritizing everything. We must simply expend a small amount of initial energy to create the routine, and then all that is left to do is follow it. There is a huge body of scientific research to explain the mechanism by which routine enables difficult things to become easy. One simplified explanation is that as we repeatedly do a certain task, the neurons, or nerve cells, make new connections through communication gateways called 'synapses.' With repetition, the connections strengthen and it becomes easier for the brain to activate them. For example, when you learn a new word, it takes several repetitions at various intervals for the word to be mastered. To recall the word later, you will need to activate the same synapses until eventually you know the word without consciously thinking about it. When we speak of 'music', we are easily led to believe that there is something that corresponds to that word — something out there, so to speak, just waiting for us to give it a name. But when we speak of music we are really talking about a multiplicity of activities and experiences. As a result, even though the goal each of us sought, a job offer, was not achieved, this interview stands out as one of the most memorable ones I've ever had, and it was solely because of his enthusiasm. det.korean: 반복을 통해 연결이 강해지고, 새 단어를 배울 때 여러 번의 반복이 필요하다.
det.analysis: repeat(동사) → repetitions(명사 복수형). 'several'이 앞에 있으므로 복수형 명사가 필요. 'several repetitions'(여러 번의 반복)이 올바른 형태.
det.tip: several + 복수명사. repeat → repetition(명사) → repetitions(복수)

det.korean: 발표는 흥미롭고 유용해야 하며, 강사가 전달한 내용보다 동료의 발표 내용을 더 많이 기억할 수 있다.

det.korean: 구급차 군단은 프랑스와 이탈리아 전쟁에서 대성공이었다. 많은 나라가 __________ 자체 구급차를 만들었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① raised objections(이의를 제기했다): 구급차가 대성공이었으므로 다른 나라가 '이의를 제기'하는 맥락이 아님
✅ ② followed suit(따라 했다) ←정답: 대성공 후 많은 나라가 '따라 해서' 자체 구급차를 만들었다는 원문에 정확히 일치
❌ ③ lost interest(관심을 잃었다): 대성공이라면 관심을 '잃는' 것이 아니라 따라 하는 것이 자연스러움
❌ ④ gained independence(독립을 얻었다): '독립을 얻다'는 구급차 도입 맥락과 무관
det.tip: followed suit = '따라 했다/선례를 따랐다'. 프랑스의 성공 → 다른 나라의 모방이 핵심 흐름

det.korean: 결국 의식적으로 그것에 대해 생각하지 않고도 단어를 알게 된다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① repeatedly practicing it(반복적으로 연습하기): 반복은 과정이지 최종 상태가 아님. 원문은 '의식적 사고 없이' 알게 된다는 결과를 설명
❌ ② physically writing it down(물리적으로 적기): 원문에 '적기'에 대한 언급 없음
❌ ③ actively searching for it(적극적으로 찾기): '찾기'는 원문 맥락(의식적 사고 없는 자동 회상)과 다름
✅ ④ consciously thinking about it(의식적으로 생각하기) ←정답: 반복을 통해 시냅스가 강화되면 '의식적으로 생각하지 않고도' 단어를 알게 된다는 원문에 정확히 일치
det.tip: consciously thinking about it = '의식적으로 생각하기'. 반복 학습 → 시냅스 강화 → 무의식적 회상의 과정
